flags.description: In 2011, Brazilian labor inspectors found migrant workers in slavery-like conditions (16-hour days, restricted movement) at a São Paulo workshop producing garments for Zara via a subcontracted supplier. Zara Brasil lost the resulting court case and its appeal, with the case closing in November 2017.

French anti-terrorism prosecutors opened an investigation in July 2021 into Inditex and three other multinationals over alleged profiting from Uyghur forced labor in Xinjiang supply chains; Canada's ombudsperson (CORE) opened a separate probe into Zara in November 2023 following a civil-society complaint.
